pointers.sentence: Each label loaded by `DiscoverRunner.load_tests_for_label`, and flattened into one list of tests by `iter_test_cases`, which refuses a string with a `TypeError`, a comment says to prevent an unfriendly `RecursionError` (`django/test/utils.py:iter_test_cases`).
Any other error in the import, a `SyntaxError` among them, ends the run (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.load_tests_for_label`).

A package or a directory is searched by `unittest.TestLoader.discover` for modules that match the pattern; so is `"."`, whose `TypeError` from `importlib.import_module` counts as not importable (`django/test/runner.py:try_importing`).
Its comment gives the reason: `unittest` would take the start directory itself as the top level, and break its modules' relative imports (`django/test/runner.py:find_top_level`).

After each discovery the runner sets the top level kept on its loader, `DiscoverRunner.test_loader` (`unittest.defaultTestLoader` by default), to `None`, which the comment says supports running tests from two top levels; on Python 3.14, `unittest.TestLoader.discover` already restores, on returning, the value it began with (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.load_tests_for_label`).

The decorator `tag` keeps a set of names on the class or the method as its tags attribute; where there are tags already, inherited ones too, it assigns the union, a new set, so a tagged subclass leaves its parent's alone (`django/test/utils.py:tag`).
A test that failed to load always matches: the comment's reason is to keep a syntax error, for instance, from letting tests falsely pass (`django/test/runner.py:test_match_tags`).
Django's documentation gives the reason for the order: to guarantee that every `TestCase` starts with a clean database (`docs/topics/testing/overview.txt`).
A `TransactionTestCase`, being no `TestCase`, lands in the bin of `SimpleTestCase` (`django/test/runner.py:reorder_tests`).

`--reverse` reverses the bin's list, which stays grouped by class: the run above, reversed, began with test_rename and ended its second bin with test_register (`django/test/runner.py:reorder_test_bin`).
That is the docstring's consistency property: for one seed and key function, two sets shuffled agree in order on the items they share (`django/test/runner.py:Shuffler`).
`shuffle_tests` shuffles each class's tests by their ids, then the classes by module and qualified name, so a class's tests stay together (`django/test/runner.py:shuffle_tests`).
